td_005_executive_decision.issue: DL-012: 140 clone items in Pack C/D Section E. 28 clone groups × 5 items each.

A_archive.action: Mark 112 clones as Archived. Keep 28 seeds active.
A_archive.risk: Reduces total item count from 2,540 to 2,428. Sections E in Packs C/D thin.
A_archive.benefit: Fast. No content modifications. 0 risk of introducing new defects.

B_rekey.action: Assign unique UniqueConceptKey to distinguish genuinely independent items.
B_rekey.risk: Requires Content Board review of each clone group. Moderate effort. Potential for metadata errors.
B_rekey.benefit: Preserves all 140 items. Differentiates which clones are truly redundant vs independently authored.

rationale: Template-rotation authoring is prohibited by U-R5 for all new content. Keeping clones preserves a pattern the architecture has explicitly deprecated.
Archiving 112 clones reduces item count by 4.6% — minimal blueprint coverage impact.
Option A has zero risk of introducing new defects. Option B requires per-item metadata updates on 140 items.
The 28 seed items remain active and certifiable. Clones provide zero additional pedagogical value beyond their seeds.
This decision aligns with the stewardship era's mandate: protect the architecture, don't redesign it.
